data.description:
## Description

**What**: Hook the `transition closed` and archive lifecycle paths to remove the per-ticket scratch directory.

**Why**: sc-4 and sc-5 share the same cleanup hook surface; combined to avoid duplicate plumbing.

**Scope**:
- IN: close-transition hook removes the per-ticket scratch directory; archive flow removes the per-ticket scratch directory; idempotent (no error if directory absent); cleanup logged on success and on failure.
- OUT: CLI itself (separate story), migration of call sites (separate story), gitignore isolation (separate story).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, on `dso ticket transition <id> <status> closed`, the per-ticket scratch directory is removed (or no-op if absent)
  ← Satisfies: sc-4
- When this story is complete, on archive of a ticket, the per-ticket scratch directory is removed (or no-op if absent)
  ← Satisfies: sc-5
- When this story is complete, cleanup is idempotent: repeated close or archive of the same ticket id never errors on missing directory
  ← Satisfies: sc-4
- When this story is complete, cleanup events are logged with the ticket id and removed-path so the audit trail shows when scratch was reclaimed
  ← Satisfies: sc-5
- When this story is complete, cleanup failures (permission denied, dir locked, etc.) are logged at WARN level with the ticket id and underlying error, and a structured marker is recorded so the orphaned scratch dir is enumerable by a follow-up sweep
  ← Satisfies: sc-4
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
  ← Satisfies: sc-4

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Cleanup must not block the transition itself — a cleanup failure warns and records an orphan marker but does not roll back the status change.
- [Recoverability] Once cleanup runs the data is gone; confirm there is no scenario where a closed-then-reopened ticket needs prior scratch contents.
- [Integration] Cleanup walks the per-ticket scratch directory regardless of key namespace, so namespace changes from the CLI / migration stories do not affect this story — confirm by including a multi-key fixture in the cleanup test.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a ticket-system operator, I want scratch storage automatically cleaned up on close and archive, so that completed tickets do not accrete orphaned handoff data
